source.title: Prototype-Based Multiple Instance Learning for Gigapixel Whole Slide Image Classification
source.authors: Su-Su Sun; D. van Midden; Geert Litjens; Christian F. Baumgartner

page_placements.theme: Dictionary geometry, stability and utilization depend on training

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates the semantic interpretability of SAE-discovered features, which bears on the semantic-unit aspect of V5, but does not test superposition geometry or capacity competition.
record.gate_note: The reported SAE sparsity statistics and concept counts are recorded as findings about pathology-image embeddings, not as tests of the LLM-specific V4 or the toy-network claims. Classification results and the removal of named artifacts do not test superposition. The reported human assessment of whether SAE concepts are monosemantic bears on part of V5; it does not establish feature completeness, stability, or canonical status.
record.test_reason: The study uses an L1 SAE on frozen CONCH pathology-image embeddings as a tool to build concept inputs for an interpretable MIL classifier. Its main results are its own method's classification performance and an artifact-removal intervention. The pathologist's monosemanticity shares (75%, 86%) measure the semantic interpretability of SAE latents. That is a related but different construct from V5's claim that SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units of the model's representation. The study has no LLM setting (V4), no toy models (V1), no capacity test (V2, V3) and no dimensionality test (V6).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that the SAE learns sparse, human-interpretable pathology concepts, though a certain number of neurons remain polysemantic and warrant future work. ProtoMIL built on these concepts matches state-of-the-art MIL classification performance. It also allows intervention that removes spurious artifact concepts while keeping performance.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains an L1-regularized SAE on frozen CONCH pathology-image embeddings and uses its activations in a WSI classifier. It does not reproduce the original toy-network setup or test its superposition geometry.

fits_no_version.finding: A pathologist judged 75% (Camelyon16) and 86% (PANDA) of active SAE concepts monosemantic. The authors state that some SAE neurons remain polysemantic.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE latents trained on pathology foundation-model embeddings are mostly, but not all, judged monosemantic by a domain expert.

fits_no_version.finding: With lambda=3e-4 and 2048 latents, the SAE averaged 10 nonzero values per vector. Only 74 of the 2048 latents were ever active across 7.7M patches.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAEs on 512-d pathology image embeddings learn a small set of active sparse concepts, with most latents dead.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Medical Image Computing and Computer-Assisted Intervention (MICCAI), 2025
record.problems: The human interpretability assessment is reported without a stated rubric, rater count, or uncertainty. The study does not test feature completeness, stability, or canonical status, or any superposition geometry.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, overlap geometry or sparsity transition.
All: no test of capacity competition.
All: the study does not examine the causes of polysemantic latents.
All: no LLM. The SAE recovering sparse codes in a vision encoder is assumed, not tested against neuron baselines.
Completeness, stability across seeds or sizes, and canonicity were not tested. Only interpretability shares were reported.
All: the dimensionality of features is not examined.

record.verdict_notes: This is a MICCAI methods paper. The SAE is used as a concept-discovery tool. The interpretability judgements are qualitative and come from a single pathologist, with no rubric or uncertainty reported. The reader's tranche T2 and its V5 limits_scope label are dropped: the monosemanticity share does not measure what V5 names.

versions.untested_parts: No toy-network test of feature overlap, near-orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry.
No test of capacity competition, dedicated dimensions for important features, or polysemanticity caused by limited capacity.
No test of whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure.
The study concerns pathology image embeddings, not LLMs; it does not test feature spread across neurons in LLMs.
The study assesses human-interpreted semantic coherence of discovered concepts, but does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of the model's representation.
No test of whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

relation.reason: Applies SAE concept discovery to frozen CONCH image embeddings without testing superposition geometry, capacity explanations, dictionary completeness or stability, or feature dimensionality. V4 specifically concerns LLMs.

tranche.reason: Uses SAE concepts as inputs to a pathology classifier. Sparsity and pathologist interpretability evaluations characterize the tool; they do not test the listed claim versions.

source_check.notes: The statement's 7.7M patches is the sum of the reported 3M and 4.7M. The 74 activated concepts are an aggregate across the SAE training set, not a per-dataset count.
